title: In 2 Kings 3 How Does Jehoshaphats Character Influence The Decisions Made In This Chapter
paragraphs: Jehoshaphat's Character and Its Influence in 2 Kings 3

The story in 2 Kings 3 offers a fascinating look at how the godly character of Jehoshaphat, king of Judah, impacts the course of events when Israel, Judah, and Edom join forces against Moab. This study will examine the narrative, highlight Jehoshaphat’s spiritual qualities, and explore how his influence shapes key decisions in this dramatic episode.
Background: The Setting of 2 Kings 3

After the death of Ahab, his son Jehoram becomes king of Israel. Moab, long subjugated to Israel, rebels. In response, Jehoram seeks military support from Jehoshaphat, king of Judah, and the king of Edom. This coalition embarks on a campaign against Moab, but soon faces a crisis: they run out of water in the wilderness (2 Kings 3:9).
Jehoshaphat’s Character: A Man Who Seeks God

Jehoshaphat is consistently portrayed in Scripture as a king who fears the Lord and seeks His guidance (2 Chronicles 17:3-4). Even amid political and military alliances, Jehoshaphat’s pattern is to inquire of the Lord before acting. This godliness is evident in 2 Kings 3.

But Jehoshaphat said, Is there not here a prophet of Jehovah, that we may inquire of Jehovah by him? And one of the king of Israel’s servants answered and said, Here is Elisha the son of Shaphat, who poured water on the hands of Elijah. - 2 Kings 3:11 ASV
Jehoshaphat’s instinct, when faced with a dire situation, is not to rely on political power or human wisdom, but to seek a word from God. This reveals both humility and spiritual sensitivity.
Influence on Decision-Making
Jehoshaphat’s presence and character profoundly influence the events in three key ways:
Prompting Spiritual Inquiry:

When the kings are faced with a logistical crisis, Jehoshaphat is the only one to suggest seeking God’s guidance. This is a turning point, as Jehoram’s initial reaction is to blame God for their predicament (2 Kings 3:10). Jehoshaphat’s suggestion leads them to Elisha, the prophet of the Lord.
Receiving God’s Provision:
Elisha is willing to speak only because of Jehoshaphat’s presence, not out of regard for Jehoram, who was an idolatrous king. Elisha says:

And Elisha said, As Jehovah of hosts liveth, before whom I stand, surely, were it not that I regard the presence of Jehoshaphat the king of Judah, I would not look toward thee, nor see thee. - 2 Kings 3:14 ASV
Because of Jehoshaphat, the coalition receives God’s miraculous provision of water and the promise of victory.
Demonstrating the Blessing of Righteous Association:

Jehoshaphat’s faithfulness brings blessing to the wider group. His godliness stands in contrast to the spiritual compromise of the northern kingdom. The favor of God on Jehoshaphat’s life serves as a channel of grace, even to those less deserving.
Lessons for Today
God honors those who seek Him: Jehoshaphat’s example encourages believers to make seeking God’s will a priority in every challenge (Matthew 6:33).
Our faithfulness can impact others: God often blesses groups, families, or communities because of the presence of even one faithful person (Genesis 18:32).

Be careful in alliances: While Jehoshaphat’s influence is positive here, his alliances with ungodly kings (see also 2 Chronicles 19:2) sometimes bring danger. Seeking God’s guidance is crucial before entering into partnerships.
Christ-Centered Insight

Ultimately, Jehoshaphat points us to the necessity of seeking God’s word above all else. In Christ, we have the perfect mediator and the living Word (John 1:14). Just as God delivered the coalition for Jehoshaphat’s sake, so in Christ, God delivers all who trust in Him by grace through faith (Ephesians 2:8-9).
Related Questions You Might Ask:
Why did Jehoshaphat ally himself with ungodly kings?
What does it mean to seek the Lord in decision making?
How does God bless others through the faithfulness of one person?
What lessons can we learn from Jehoshaphat’s life?
